phrases.english: Shall we go out for dinner tonight?

phrases.latin: vēnit ad nōs Cicerō tuus ad cēnam, cum Pompōnia forīs cēnāret
phrases.english: your boy Cicero came to us for dinner, as Pomponia was dining out

phrases.latin: cūrā ut valeās; id forīs cēnitandō facillimē cōnsequēre
phrases.english: look after your health; you’ll manage that most easily by dining out often

phrases.latin: Ad cēnam hercle aliō prōmīsī forās. — Quid, forās? — Forās hercle vērō. — Quī malum tibi lassō libet forīs cēnāre?
phrases.english: I’ve promised to go out to dinner somewhere else, by Hercules. — What, out? — Out, by Hercules, yes. — Why the devil, tired as you are, do you want to eat out?

sources: Lewis & Short: foris
John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 71, 304, 308.
Cicero, Letters to Friends 9.24.3; Letters to his brother Quintus 3.1.19.
